header.running_head: The Practices of Nabi ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) with Regard to Clothing

blocks.text: The Practices of Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) and Hadhrat Asmaa (RA) With Regard to Clothing

Hadhrat Katheer bin Ubayd narrates that when he once went to Ummul Mu'mineen Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), she told him to wait until she completed stitching her old garment. As he waited, he remarked, "O Ummul Mu'mineen! If I went out and informed the people about this, they would regard it as miserliness from your side (thinking that you are too miserly to buy new clothes)." Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) said, "Do as you see fit. The person who does not wear old clothes does not deserve new clothes (and may not have them in the Aakhirah)." [^2]

Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed reports that when someone entered Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA)'s room as she was stitching her old garment, he remarked, "O Ummul Mu'mineen! Has Allaah not granted an abundance of wealth (to buy new clothing rather than patch old clothing)?" Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) replied, "Leave us alone! The person who does not wear old clothes does not deserve new clothes." [^3]

When Hadhrat Mundhir bin Zubayr (RA) arrived from Iraq, (his mother) Hadhrat Asmaa bint Abu Bakr (RA) had already become blind. He sent for her delicate and exquisite garments made in Marw and Quw and when she felt it, she exclaimed, "Alas! Send this clothing back to him." Hadhrat Mundhir (RA) felt hurt about it and said, "Dear mother! The garments are not transparent." She replied, "Even though they are not transparent, they are revealing." When he then bought for her common garments made in Marw and Quw, she accepted them saying, "It is these types of garments that you should give me to wear." [^4]
The Practice of Hadhrat Umar (RA) with Clothing

Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that a woman once came to Hadhrat Umar (RA) saying, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! My upper garment is all tattered." "Have I not given you anything to wear?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked. "You have given me," she replied, "but it has torn." Hadhrat Umar (RA) immediately sent for an exquisite upper garment and some thread to be given to her. He then said to her, "Wear that (old clothing) when you are making bread and cooking and then wear this (new garment) once you have finished. Those not wearing old clothing do not deserve new clothes." [^5]
